question: Measuring a patient's satisfaction with a counselling session (Level 1 Kirkpatrick) is sufficient evidence that the counselling produced the desired behaviour change.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Level 1 Kirkpatrick measures participant reaction (satisfaction), not behaviour change. To confirm behaviour change you need Level 3 assessment, such as follow-up observation or self-report of practice change weeks later.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually, this statement is FALSE. Level 1 (Reaction) only captures how participants felt about the session. Behaviour change is Level 3 (Behaviour) and health outcome improvement is Level 4 (Results). Satisfaction scores do not predict behaviour change.
